chunk_findings.detail: `_linked` deduplicates against any open bug whose summary merely contains the failing test ids, without requiring the bug to be a baseline-red bug. Given an unrelated open bug with summary `"Investigate test_login regression"` and a baseline-red failure whose ids are `["test_login"]`, the check `all(i in b.summary for i in ids)` returns true, `_linked` returns that bug, and `_file` is skipped. The resulting baseline-red event is therefore not filed or counted as a bug tagged `baseline-red`, contrary to the stated dedup/tagging behavior.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/api/gate_baseline.py:_linked

chunk_findings.detail: The test-id match is substring-based, so a bug that names only a longer test id can incorrectly satisfy a request for a shorter id. Given failing ids `["test_a", "test_ab"]` and an open bug summary `"test_ab fails on base"`, the condition `all(i in b.summary for i in ids)` is true because `"test_a"` is a substring of `"test_ab"`; `_linked` returns that bug and suppresses filing for `test_a`, even though the bug does not name `test_a` as a separate failing test.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/api/gate_baseline.py:_linked

chunk_findings.detail: `notify` records the acceptance as “told” via `PO.record_auto` before sending the coordinator inbox message, and it ignores the result of `LR.notify`. `_said` deduplicates on the approvals-log entry created by `record_auto`. Given a transient inbox failure (for example, `LR.notify` raises or returns false after the log entry is written), the gate acceptance is already marked as said; on the next gate run or completion, `_said` returns true and `notify` returns false without retrying the coordinator message. The coordinator can therefore never receive the required notice even though the system reports it as told.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/api/gate_baseline_notice.py:notify

chunk_findings.detail: The rate-warning check treats only exactly `0` as “never note”, but `baseline_red_rate_warn` is an unrestricted int knob. If an operator sets `gates.baseline_red_rate_warn` to any negative value (for example `-1`), then `not cfg.gates.baseline_red_rate_warn` is false and `recent < cfg.gates.baseline_red_rate_warn` is also false even when `recent == 0`, so `_red_base_note` returns the “the base branch is red: 0 baseline-red partial(s) …” doctor note. A non-positive threshold should disable the note (or the knob should reject negatives), not cause a false base-red warning.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/services/approvals/audit.py:_red_base_note

chunk_findings.detail: The automatic-acceptance path is not bound to the current measured outcome. `accepted()` returns `True` whenever stored evidence has `baseline.auto.accepted is True` and the knob is on, but it never checks `digest(it, gate)` (or any equivalent stored measurement state), unlike the person-approval path immediately below which calls `AP.check(..., digest(it, gate))`. Given a `gate run` that records a baseline-red automatic acceptance for commit A, an agent can then edit the item (for example, add a new failure in a changed file) without re-running the gate; the old `baseline.auto` evidence remains, `refusal()` is still empty, and `accepted(state, it, gate, cfg)` still returns `True`. Completion would therefore accept the new partial outcome as automatically accepted even though the current code was never measured against the baseline and may contain a new failure. This violates D-baseline-red-auto-accept / D-accept-baseline-red-partial because the acceptance is not tied to the current partial outcome.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/services/gate_accept.py:accepted / auto_ids

chunk_findings.detail: `cache_store` cannot record a valid empty baseline result. If the base full-suite run measures zero failing ids, the caller has no way to persist “this base was measured and has no baseline failures”: `cache_store(repo, sha, {}, ttl)` returns immediately without writing, and `cache_load(repo, sha, ttl)` also returns `{}` for a missing/expired cache. Given a clean baseline on base sha `abc123`, a later item that calls `cache_load` sees `{}` and cannot distinguish “no cache” from “cached clean baseline”, so it must re-run the base (or treat the measurement as missing), contrary to the stated “one full-suite result per base sha … measuring costs a comparison, not a run” behavior.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/services/gates/baseline.py:cache_store

chunk_findings.detail: The baseline cache is keyed only by the repository and resolved base sha (`BL.cache_load(repo, sha, ttl_s)` / `BL.cache_store(repo, sha, ...)`), but the measured result is produced by the current gate definition: `run(replace(gdef, command=cmd), tree.path)`. If two invocations have the same base sha but different `gdef.command` values, the cached statuses from one command are reused as if they were the baseline result for the other. For example, a `ci` gate probe on base sha `S` runs `pytest tests/ci.py` and caches `tests/common.py::test_x` as failing. Later the `unit_tests` gate, whose command is `pytest tests/unit.py` (or whose command was changed without moving the base sha), probes the same id on the same base sha; `on_base` sees `all(i in known ...)` and returns `red: True` without running the unit_tests command on the base. If that id is actually a new failure under the unit_tests command, the acceptance logic can still accept it as baseline-red. This violates the configurable-command semantics and [r-everything-configurable]/[D-baseline-red-auto-accept]; the cache key must include the gate/command (or the cache must be produced only by a command-independent full-suite baseline run).
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/services/gates/baseline_red.py:on_base

chunk_findings.detail: The “told once” test does not actually verify “once” after the repeated gate run. After the first run it checks that there is exactly one ask and one pending coordinator message, but after the second `_run(repo)` it only asserts `len(IB.pending(repo, "coordinator")) <= 2` and never reloads state to check that the ask count, bug count, or evidence bug id are unchanged. If the implementation duplicates the coordinator notification on a repeated baseline-red acceptance (for example, the ask is deduplicated but an inbox message is appended again), the test still passes because two pending messages satisfy `<= 2`; likewise, if the second run files a duplicate baseline-red bug, no assertion catches it. The stated requirement is “notice and bug filed once,” so the second run should leave exactly one notice/bug, not up to two.
chunk_findings.title: tests/test_baseline_red_auto.py:62

chunk_findings.detail: The dedup check `all(i in b.summary for i in ids)` matches raw test-id text as substrings, not as standalone test identifiers. A prior bug whose summary names `test_foo_bar` also contains the substring `test_foo`, so a new baseline-red run with `ids == ["test_foo"]` makes `_linked` return that prior bug and skip `_file`. The distinct baseline-red test `test_foo` is then never filed or tracked, violating the test-id dedup/file-once behavior.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/api/gate_baseline.py:_linked

chunk_findings.detail: `notify` persists the acceptance with `PO.record_auto(...)` before it attempts `LR.notify(...)`. If the notification adapter fails—for example the coordinator inbox is unavailable and `LR.notify` raises or returns a failure—the already-persisted approval record makes the next invocation pass the `PO.used(...) and _said(...)` dedup check and return `False`, so `LR.notify` is never retried. The `_run.py` caller does not catch this, so the original gate run can error after already recording the accepted baseline-red partial, while the coordinator is never actually told.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/api/gate_baseline_notice.py:notify

chunk_findings.detail: The new helper calls `clock.epoch(r["answered_at"], default=0.0)`, but the diff does not add an import for `clock`; the visible import context only adds `timedelta` next to `import time`. Once an automatic baseline-red acceptance record exists, `_red_base_note` reaches the `clock.epoch(...)` expression during `ddflow doctor` and raises `NameError: name 'clock' is not defined`, so the doctor note/crash path activates exactly when this feature is used.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/services/approvals/audit.py:_red_base_note

chunk_findings.detail: The auto-acceptance knob fallback is `"off"` via `getattr(cfg.gates, "baseline_red_auto", "off")`, but the stated default for `[gates].baseline_red_auto` is `"on"` [D-baseline-red-auto-accept]. Given a `cfg` whose `gates` section lacks this knob (for example a config object built before the new upgrade template, or a minimal test config), `auto_ids` returns `[]` and `accepted` falls through to person-only `AP.check`, so an otherwise valid, measured baseline-red partial is not auto-accepted. The fallback should be `"on"`.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/services/gate_accept.py:72

chunk_findings.detail: The baseline-red-specific explanation is appended unconditionally whenever `CN.operator_gate` returns a non-ok decision, not only when the refusal is for a baseline-red partial. A non-baseline-red gate denial such as `ddflow gate accept <item> <ordinary-gate>` will now tell the user that “A baseline-red partial needs no request” and instruct them to run the gate themselves, which is wrong and may lead them to bypass a real approval requirement. The additional text should be guarded by the condition identifying a baseline-red partial.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/services/gate_accept.py:133

chunk_findings.detail: The guard only returns `""` when `it.gate_outcome(gate) != ACCEPTABLE` or `refusal(it, gate)` is true; it never checks that the gate actually has a baseline-red measurement. For a non-baseline gate whose outcome is `ACCEPTABLE`, `refusal` is false, and whose evidence is `None` or `{}`, this function returns the baseline-red action block beginning `"; <gate> is partial and baseline-red..."`, contradicting its own docstring that says it returns `""` for any other gate. Example call: `next_step(item, "item-1", "coverage")` with `coverage` acceptable, no refusal, and no baseline evidence sends the agent a false “coverage is baseline-red / do NOT request approval” instruction.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/services/gate_accept.py:next_step

chunk_findings.detail: `cache_store` writes one `"at"` timestamp for the whole cache file and refreshes it on every merge, and `cache_load` uses that timestamp for every test id. A new measurement of one id extends the TTL for all previously measured ids without re-measuring them. Input: with `baseline_cache_ttl_s=60`, store `test_a: true` at t=0; store `test_b: false` at t=59; then `cache_load(..., now=100)` returns `test_a` as fresh even though the `test_a` measurement is 100s old and should have expired. An old baseline-red result for `test_a` can then make `auto_decision` accept an item failure even when a fresh base run would no longer fail, so the TTL knob does not actually bound the age of cached baseline measurements.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/services/gates/baseline.py cache_store/cache_load

chunk_findings.detail: This new module takes the clock directly with `time.time()` and reaches the filesystem directly with `Path.read_text` and `path.parent.mkdir`, rather than going through a port in `ddflow/adapters`. The recorded r-adapters rule explicitly calls out clocks and filesystem layout as external dependencies; this direct use means tests cannot substitute a fake clock/filesystem for this logic, a swap must touch more than the adapter, and the advisory is violated.
chunk_findings.title: [r-adapters] ddflow/services/gates/baseline.py cache_load/cache_store

chunk_findings.detail: The test claims that a second identical `_run(repo)` “says nothing more” and the test name says the acceptance is “told once,” but the assertion only checks `len(IB.pending(repo, "coordinator")) <= 2`. If the implementation erroneously posts a duplicate coordinator inbox message on every gate run, the second run makes the length 2 and the test still passes. The assertion should be `== 1` to catch duplicate notifications.
chunk_findings.title: tests/test_baseline_red_auto.py:62

chunk_findings.detail: `found["auto"] = BL.auto_decision(...)` is computed only after `_linked` / `_file`, and no branch uses it to prevent filing or linking a baseline-red bug. For example, with `[gates].baseline_red_auto = "off"` (person-only), or with it `"on"` but one failing id is in a file the item changed, `found["red"]` can still be true; `apply` still calls `_file`, creating a bug tagged `baseline-red`, then records `found["auto"]` as false. The acceptance decision must be made before any bug is filed/linked (and before returning the accepted partial reason), so a blocked acceptance can still produce an automatic baseline-red bug.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/api/gate_baseline.py:apply

chunk_findings.detail: The duplicate-suppression key is the rendered notice text, but `notice_text` truncates the failing-id list at `SHOWN = 8`. If the acceptance has more than eight ids, a change to any id beyond the first eight that leaves the total count unchanged produces exactly the same text, so `_said` treats the notice as already said and `notify` returns `False` without sending a new inbox message or recording a new log entry. For example, first acceptance has `auto.ids = ["a","b","c","d","e","f","g","h","x"]`; a later acceptance has `auto.ids = ["a","b","c","d","e","f","g","h","y"]`. Both render as `...: a, b, c, d, e, f, g, h (+1 more) fail ...`, so the second run is suppressed even though the evidence `ids` changed, contradicting the stated “told once per recorded outcome and failing ids” behavior.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/api/gate_baseline_notice.py:_said

chunk_findings.detail: The recorded reason is built as `R.render(canon, text, cfg.approvals.reason_chars) + f"\n  accepted automatically: {rule_id}"`, so the configured `reason_chars` limit is applied only to the first part of the text. The final stored reason can therefore exceed `cfg.approvals.reason_chars`, and if the approvals log re-truncates the stored reason to that limit, the appended `accepted automatically` marker (and possibly the baseline-red ids in `text`) can be cut off. For example, with `cfg.approvals.reason_chars=40` and a 45-character baseline-red reason containing test ids, the rendered part is 40 characters, the suffix makes the stored reason longer than 40, and a 40-character display truncation loses the fact that the acceptance was automatic. This violates the configured reason limit [r-everything-configurable].
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/services/approvals/policy.py:record_auto

chunk_findings.detail: The added guidance in the `ValueError` is emitted whenever `refusal(it, gate)` is empty, not only when automatic acceptance would actually happen. For example, if a gate has a measured baseline-red partial but `[gates].baseline_red_auto` is `off` (or auto-acceptance was blocked because a failing id is in a changed/imported file), `refusal` can still return empty while `auto_ids(...)` returns `[]`. An agent request that fails `CN.operator_gate` then receives “A baseline-red partial needs no request: `gate run` accepts it itself”, even though `gate run` will not accept it. That contradicts D-baseline-red-auto-accept and can cause an agent to loop instead of fixing the failure or obtaining a person approval.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/services/gate_accept.py:request_approval

chunk_findings.detail: Automatic acceptance is not tied to the current gate/item state. `accepted(state, it, gate, cfg)` returns the automatic verdict solely from stored evidence `baseline.auto.accepted` and the current config, ignoring `state` and `digest(it, gate)`, while the person path requires `AP.check(... digest(it, gate))`. If `gate run` records `baseline.auto.accepted: true` for ids `[t1]`, then the item is changed so that `t1` is now in a changed file (or a new failing test appears) and the gate evidence is not rewritten, `accepted` still returns `True`. This can let `complete` settle a stale partial, violating D-accept-baseline-red-partial’s requirement that the *current* partial be measured as baseline-red and D-baseline-red-auto-accept’s changed-file/import-graph check.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/services/gate_accept.py:auto_ids

chunk_findings.detail: `cache_store` is documented as best-effort, but its merge step trusts the existing cache file’s shape. If a local cache file contains valid JSON whose `ids` value is not a mapping (for example `{"ids": []}`) or whose entries are malformed mappings (for example `{"ids": {"a": {}}}`), the merge code raises `AttributeError` from `held.items()` or `KeyError` from `v[1]`, neither of which is caught by the outer `except (OSError, ValueError, IndexError, TypeError)`. For example, with `.ddflow/local/baseline/<sha>.<cmd>.json` containing `{"ids": []}`, calling `cache_store(repo, sha, {"tests/test_a.py::t": True}, ttl_s=60)` crashes instead of returning and forcing a rerun.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/services/gates/baseline.py:cache_store

chunk_findings.detail: The cache uses `time.time()` directly for timestamps and TTL checks, bypassing the project’s clock adapter required by [r-adapters] (“clocks” are listed as external dependencies that must go through a port). This also makes TTL enforcement depend on wall-clock time: if the system clock moves backward after a cache entry is written, `clock_now - float(v[1])` is negative and the entry is treated as fresh, so `[gates].baseline_cache_ttl_s` does not expire it. `cache_store` additionally has no injectable clock, so expiration cannot be tested deterministically.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/services/gates/baseline.py:cache_load/cache_store

chunk_findings.detail: When a chunk run returns outcome `"failed"` and no `failed_tests_more`, the code stores `False` for every id in that chunk that is not listed in `failed_tests`. That is only sound if the command executed every selected id. A gate command that stops on the first failure (`pytest -x` / `--maxfail=1`) or times out does not. With an empty baseline cache, `gdef.command = "pytest -x"`, and current failing ids `["test_a", "test_b"]` where both fail on the base, the single chunk runs `pytest -x test_a test_b`; `test_a` fails, `test_b` is not run, evidence has `failed_tests=["test_a"]` and no `failed_tests_more`. The code caches `test_b` as not failing on the base. Later, for an item failing only `test_b`, the cached branch sees `test_b` known `False` and returns `red=False`, permanently blocking a valid baseline-red acceptance. The unrun probe should be treated as unavailable/unknown, not as a passed baseline test.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/services/gates/baseline_red.py:on_base (chunk loop, `known.update` / `BL.cache_store`)

chunk_findings.detail: `_ci_baseline_red` returns true whenever the ci gate’s stored evidence has `baseline.red is True`, without checking that that evidence is for the current tree/base or that the probe actually ran for this tree. `scope` then skips `_ci_not_passed_here(cfg, it, tree)`, which is the tree-aware fallback. Concrete failure: an item previously ran ci on tree T1 and left `ci.outcome == "partial"` with `ci.evidence = {"baseline": {"red": True}}`; the item is then checked on a new tree T2 (or after the base moved) with no ci run for T2. `_ci_not_passed_here` would return a reason because the ci gate did not pass “here”, but `red` is true, so `scope` returns a selected scope for the unit_tests gate instead of the full/waiting scope. The unit_tests gate can then run only the selected scope and miss failures outside it, treating a stale/unavailable baseline probe as accepted.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/services/testscope.py:_ci_baseline_red

chunk_findings.detail: The `new` value is written as `"\"on\""`, which TOML parses to the literal string `"on"` including quote characters, not the intended knob value `on`. A consumer that uses this field as the default value or validates it against the documented `on|off` set will not match: `change["new"] == "on"` is false. The change therefore encodes a broken default for the automatic acceptance knob, so the described default-on behavior is not actually represented.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/templates/upgrade/unreleased/knob_added.gates.baseline_red_auto.toml:6

chunk_findings.detail: The `new` value is written as `"\"coordinator\""`, which TOML parses to the literal string `"coordinator"` with embedded quotes, not the recipient name `coordinator`. If the notification code or upgrade consumer compares this value to the coordinator inbox or writes it as the config value, it will not match the intended recipient. The neighboring integer `baseline_red_rate_warn` entry uses an unquoted `10`, indicating `new` is meant to be the actual value rather than a quoted TOML source fragment.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/templates/upgrade/unreleased/knob_added.gates.baseline_red_notify_to.toml:6

chunk_findings.detail: The fake baseline measurement returned by the monkeypatched `BR.on_base` is internally inconsistent with the contract exercised elsewhere in this file: it returns `{"red": False, "still_failing": ids[:-1]}`. A non-empty `still_failing` list should imply a red baseline (`test_the_base_is_run_once_per_sha_and_shared` asserts `red` is true when the baseline run has failing tests, while `test_a_run_that_could_not_run_is_not_cached_and_never_red` asserts `red` is false only for an unavailable run). If `gate_baseline.apply` honors the `red` flag, it will not treat this as a baseline-red comparison and will likely mark all current failing ids as new, so the assertion `ev["baseline"]["new_failures"] == [ids[-1]]` fails. If `apply` ignores `red` and uses `still_failing` anyway, the test passes but does not actually exercise the intended “baseline-red ci with one new failure blocks” path.
chunk_findings.title: tests/test_baseline_red_auto.py:test_ci_with_a_failure_not_on_the_base_stays_failed_and_says_so

chunk_findings.detail: The fixture invokes `subprocess.run(["git", ...])` directly to add and commit the fake project, bypassing the project’s adapter/port discipline for external dependencies and subprocess tools. This violates [r-adapters], which requires external dependencies (explicitly including git and subprocess tools) to go through `ddflow/adapters` ports and encourages tests to use fakes instead of real subprocesses.
chunk_findings.title: tests/test_baseline_red_auto.py:_ci_project

chunk_findings.detail: The new baseline write has no `full` guard. `cirun` is explicitly intended to support partial runs (`full=False`), and in a partial run `res.failures` only contains the tests that the partial scope happened to execute. The block treats that subset as a full-suite baseline by calling `BL.write_full(repo, res.sha, everyone)`. Concrete failure: a partial run on base sha `B` runs tests only for changed file `a.py`, fails `test_a`, and never runs `test_b`, which is also failing in the full suite on `B`; the cache for `B` becomes `[test_a]`. A later item based on `B` whose only failure is `test_b` is therefore blocked instead of accepted as baseline-red, violating the “one full-suite result per base sha” invariant and the promised `subset of baseline failures` acceptance.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/api/cirun.py:158-165

chunk_findings.detail: `_names` does not enforce the same boundary after the id as before it: the negative lookbehind forbids `.` and `/`, but the negative lookahead `(?![\w\]\[:-])` omits both. Concretely, `_names("test.py::test[param.with.dot]", "test.py::test[param]")` returns True because the shorter id is matched at the start and the following `.` is allowed. A pytest parameterized test can have both `test.py::test[param]` and `test.py::test[param.with.dot]` as distinct node ids; an open bug mentioning only the longer id would be treated as already naming the shorter failing id, so `_linked` reuses the wrong bug and never files the baseline-red bug for the real `test[param]` failure. The trailing boundary must forbid the same id characters as the leading boundary.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/api/gate_baseline.py:_names

chunk_findings.detail: When `notify_auto` fails to send the inbox message because `LR.notify` returns a non-empty `why` (e.g., the coordinator inbox adapter is temporarily unavailable), `notify_auto` returns `False` without recording anything, and this return value is discarded here. The gate outcome has already been recorded as accepted-baseline-red, so there is no later call to `notify_auto` unless the gate is run again. In that environment the item is accepted without the required coordinator notification, and the intended retry represented by `notify_auto`’s `False` is never acted upon.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/api/gates/_run.py:481

chunk_findings.detail: When `[gates].baseline_red_auto` is `"off"` (person-only mode) and a measured baseline-red partial is still unsettled, `refusal(it, gate)` is still falsy, so this branch appends “`gate run` accepts it itself”. But `auto_ids` only auto-accepts when the knob is `"on"`; with it off, `gate run` will not accept itself and a person must approve. This makes the error string instruct the agent to re-run a gate that will still not settle, which is wrong for that configuration.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/services/gate_accept.py:150

chunk_findings.detail: `cache_load`, `cache_store`, and `write_full` access the filesystem and system clock directly (`time.time`, `Path.read_text`, `Path.mkdir`, `atomic_write`, `fsio.ensure_ignored_dir`) instead of going through a port in `ddflow/adapters`. [r-adapters] says filesystem layout and clocks are external dependencies that must go through adapters. This implementation cannot be swapped for a fake, and the shared `.ddflow/local/baseline` read-modify-write cache has no adapter-mediated serialization, so parallel stock items can lose cache updates.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/services/gates/baseline.py:31-80

chunk_findings.detail: When the per-chunk run returns `("failed", {"failed_tests": []})` (for example a collection/infrastructure failure where no test IDs could be captured), `failing_here` is empty, and the condition `outcome in ("passed", "failed") and not ev.get("failed_tests_more")` is true, so the code stores every id in that chunk as `False` in the baseline cache. This turns an unavailable base measurement into a cached “these tests pass on the base” verdict. Later calls with those ids hit the all-cached branch and return `red=False` without re-running, blocking baseline-red auto-accept until cache TTL expiry or base movement. The code’s own comment says a run that could not run says nothing about the base; such a result must not be cached as a pass.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/services/gates/baseline_red.py:on_base

chunk_findings.detail: The new test helper invokes `subprocess.run(["git", "-C", str(repo), "add", "-A"], check=True)` and a matching `git commit` directly rather than going through the ddflow/adapters port for git/subprocess. This violates r-adapters, which requires subprocess/git access through a port and says tests should use a fake instead of a real subprocess. In an environment where the `git` CLI is absent or no user identity is configured, the commit step raises `CalledProcessError` and `_ci_project` fails, even though the code under test would otherwise behave correctly.
chunk_findings.title: tests/test_baseline_red_auto.py:_ci_project [r-adapters]

chunk_findings.detail: `_path` computes `digest(command)[:12]` on line 33, but `digest` from `ddflow.core.digest` (content_digest) expects a file path or bytes, not a string command. Passing a string like `""` or `"pytest tests/"` will raise a TypeError when it attempts to open or process the argument as bytes/Path.

chunk_findings.detail: `_linked` deduplicates against any open bug whose summary merely contains the failing test ids, without requiring the bug to be a baseline-red bug. Given an unrelated open bug with summary `"Investigate test_login regression"` and a baseline-red failure whose ids are `["test_login"]`, the check `all(i in b.summary for i in ids)` returns true, `_linked` returns that bug, and `_file` is skipped. The resulting baseline-red event is therefore not filed or counted as a bug tagged `baseline-red`, contrary to the stated dedup/tagging behavior.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/api/gate_baseline.py:_linked

chunk_findings.detail: The test-id match is substring-based, so a bug that names only a longer test id can incorrectly satisfy a request for a shorter id. Given failing ids `["test_a", "test_ab"]` and an open bug summary `"test_ab fails on base"`, the condition `all(i in b.summary for i in ids)` is true because `"test_a"` is a substring of `"test_ab"`; `_linked` returns that bug and suppresses filing for `test_a`, even though the bug does not name `test_a` as a separate failing test.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/api/gate_baseline.py:_linked

chunk_findings.detail: `notify` records the acceptance as “told” via `PO.record_auto` before sending the coordinator inbox message, and it ignores the result of `LR.notify`. `_said` deduplicates on the approvals-log entry created by `record_auto`. Given a transient inbox failure (for example, `LR.notify` raises or returns false after the log entry is written), the gate acceptance is already marked as said; on the next gate run or completion, `_said` returns true and `notify` returns false without retrying the coordinator message. The coordinator can therefore never receive the required notice even though the system reports it as told.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/api/gate_baseline_notice.py:notify

chunk_findings.detail: The rate-warning check treats only exactly `0` as “never note”, but `baseline_red_rate_warn` is an unrestricted int knob. If an operator sets `gates.baseline_red_rate_warn` to any negative value (for example `-1`), then `not cfg.gates.baseline_red_rate_warn` is false and `recent < cfg.gates.baseline_red_rate_warn` is also false even when `recent == 0`, so `_red_base_note` returns the “the base branch is red: 0 baseline-red partial(s) …” doctor note. A non-positive threshold should disable the note (or the knob should reject negatives), not cause a false base-red warning.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/services/approvals/audit.py:_red_base_note

chunk_findings.detail: The automatic-acceptance path is not bound to the current measured outcome. `accepted()` returns `True` whenever stored evidence has `baseline.auto.accepted is True` and the knob is on, but it never checks `digest(it, gate)` (or any equivalent stored measurement state), unlike the person-approval path immediately below which calls `AP.check(..., digest(it, gate))`. Given a `gate run` that records a baseline-red automatic acceptance for commit A, an agent can then edit the item (for example, add a new failure in a changed file) without re-running the gate; the old `baseline.auto` evidence remains, `refusal()` is still empty, and `accepted(state, it, gate, cfg)` still returns `True`. Completion would therefore accept the new partial outcome as automatically accepted even though the current code was never measured against the baseline and may contain a new failure. This violates D-baseline-red-auto-accept / D-accept-baseline-red-partial because the acceptance is not tied to the current partial outcome.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/services/gate_accept.py:accepted / auto_ids

chunk_findings.detail: `cache_store` cannot record a valid empty baseline result. If the base full-suite run measures zero failing ids, the caller has no way to persist “this base was measured and has no baseline failures”: `cache_store(repo, sha, {}, ttl)` returns immediately without writing, and `cache_load(repo, sha, ttl)` also returns `{}` for a missing/expired cache. Given a clean baseline on base sha `abc123`, a later item that calls `cache_load` sees `{}` and cannot distinguish “no cache” from “cached clean baseline”, so it must re-run the base (or treat the measurement as missing), contrary to the stated “one full-suite result per base sha … measuring costs a comparison, not a run” behavior.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/services/gates/baseline.py:cache_store

chunk_findings.detail: The baseline cache is keyed only by the repository and resolved base sha (`BL.cache_load(repo, sha, ttl_s)` / `BL.cache_store(repo, sha, ...)`), but the measured result is produced by the current gate definition: `run(replace(gdef, command=cmd), tree.path)`. If two invocations have the same base sha but different `gdef.command` values, the cached statuses from one command are reused as if they were the baseline result for the other. For example, a `ci` gate probe on base sha `S` runs `pytest tests/ci.py` and caches `tests/common.py::test_x` as failing. Later the `unit_tests` gate, whose command is `pytest tests/unit.py` (or whose command was changed without moving the base sha), probes the same id on the same base sha; `on_base` sees `all(i in known ...)` and returns `red: True` without running the unit_tests command on the base. If that id is actually a new failure under the unit_tests command, the acceptance logic can still accept it as baseline-red. This violates the configurable-command semantics and [r-everything-configurable]/[D-baseline-red-auto-accept]; the cache key must include the gate/command (or the cache must be produced only by a command-independent full-suite baseline run).
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/services/gates/baseline_red.py:on_base

chunk_findings.detail: The “told once” test does not actually verify “once” after the repeated gate run. After the first run it checks that there is exactly one ask and one pending coordinator message, but after the second `_run(repo)` it only asserts `len(IB.pending(repo, "coordinator")) <= 2` and never reloads state to check that the ask count, bug count, or evidence bug id are unchanged. If the implementation duplicates the coordinator notification on a repeated baseline-red acceptance (for example, the ask is deduplicated but an inbox message is appended again), the test still passes because two pending messages satisfy `<= 2`; likewise, if the second run files a duplicate baseline-red bug, no assertion catches it. The stated requirement is “notice and bug filed once,” so the second run should leave exactly one notice/bug, not up to two.
chunk_findings.title: tests/test_baseline_red_auto.py:62

chunk_findings.detail: The dedup check `all(i in b.summary for i in ids)` matches raw test-id text as substrings, not as standalone test identifiers. A prior bug whose summary names `test_foo_bar` also contains the substring `test_foo`, so a new baseline-red run with `ids == ["test_foo"]` makes `_linked` return that prior bug and skip `_file`. The distinct baseline-red test `test_foo` is then never filed or tracked, violating the test-id dedup/file-once behavior.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/api/gate_baseline.py:_linked

chunk_findings.detail: `notify` persists the acceptance with `PO.record_auto(...)` before it attempts `LR.notify(...)`. If the notification adapter fails—for example the coordinator inbox is unavailable and `LR.notify` raises or returns a failure—the already-persisted approval record makes the next invocation pass the `PO.used(...) and _said(...)` dedup check and return `False`, so `LR.notify` is never retried. The `_run.py` caller does not catch this, so the original gate run can error after already recording the accepted baseline-red partial, while the coordinator is never actually told.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/api/gate_baseline_notice.py:notify

chunk_findings.detail: The new helper calls `clock.epoch(r["answered_at"], default=0.0)`, but the diff does not add an import for `clock`; the visible import context only adds `timedelta` next to `import time`. Once an automatic baseline-red acceptance record exists, `_red_base_note` reaches the `clock.epoch(...)` expression during `ddflow doctor` and raises `NameError: name 'clock' is not defined`, so the doctor note/crash path activates exactly when this feature is used.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/services/approvals/audit.py:_red_base_note

chunk_findings.detail: The auto-acceptance knob fallback is `"off"` via `getattr(cfg.gates, "baseline_red_auto", "off")`, but the stated default for `[gates].baseline_red_auto` is `"on"` [D-baseline-red-auto-accept]. Given a `cfg` whose `gates` section lacks this knob (for example a config object built before the new upgrade template, or a minimal test config), `auto_ids` returns `[]` and `accepted` falls through to person-only `AP.check`, so an otherwise valid, measured baseline-red partial is not auto-accepted. The fallback should be `"on"`.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/services/gate_accept.py:72

chunk_findings.detail: The baseline-red-specific explanation is appended unconditionally whenever `CN.operator_gate` returns a non-ok decision, not only when the refusal is for a baseline-red partial. A non-baseline-red gate denial such as `ddflow gate accept <item> <ordinary-gate>` will now tell the user that “A baseline-red partial needs no request” and instruct them to run the gate themselves, which is wrong and may lead them to bypass a real approval requirement. The additional text should be guarded by the condition identifying a baseline-red partial.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/services/gate_accept.py:133

chunk_findings.detail: The guard only returns `""` when `it.gate_outcome(gate) != ACCEPTABLE` or `refusal(it, gate)` is true; it never checks that the gate actually has a baseline-red measurement. For a non-baseline gate whose outcome is `ACCEPTABLE`, `refusal` is false, and whose evidence is `None` or `{}`, this function returns the baseline-red action block beginning `"; <gate> is partial and baseline-red..."`, contradicting its own docstring that says it returns `""` for any other gate. Example call: `next_step(item, "item-1", "coverage")` with `coverage` acceptable, no refusal, and no baseline evidence sends the agent a false “coverage is baseline-red / do NOT request approval” instruction.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/services/gate_accept.py:next_step

chunk_findings.detail: `cache_store` writes one `"at"` timestamp for the whole cache file and refreshes it on every merge, and `cache_load` uses that timestamp for every test id. A new measurement of one id extends the TTL for all previously measured ids without re-measuring them. Input: with `baseline_cache_ttl_s=60`, store `test_a: true` at t=0; store `test_b: false` at t=59; then `cache_load(..., now=100)` returns `test_a` as fresh even though the `test_a` measurement is 100s old and should have expired. An old baseline-red result for `test_a` can then make `auto_decision` accept an item failure even when a fresh base run would no longer fail, so the TTL knob does not actually bound the age of cached baseline measurements.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/services/gates/baseline.py cache_store/cache_load

chunk_findings.detail: This new module takes the clock directly with `time.time()` and reaches the filesystem directly with `Path.read_text` and `path.parent.mkdir`, rather than going through a port in `ddflow/adapters`. The recorded r-adapters rule explicitly calls out clocks and filesystem layout as external dependencies; this direct use means tests cannot substitute a fake clock/filesystem for this logic, a swap must touch more than the adapter, and the advisory is violated.
chunk_findings.title: [r-adapters] ddflow/services/gates/baseline.py cache_load/cache_store

chunk_findings.detail: The test claims that a second identical `_run(repo)` “says nothing more” and the test name says the acceptance is “told once,” but the assertion only checks `len(IB.pending(repo, "coordinator")) <= 2`. If the implementation erroneously posts a duplicate coordinator inbox message on every gate run, the second run makes the length 2 and the test still passes. The assertion should be `== 1` to catch duplicate notifications.
chunk_findings.title: tests/test_baseline_red_auto.py:62

chunk_findings.detail: When a ci run is fail-fast, the new code treats the failures present in the partial output as the complete failing-id list. `everyone = [f["id"] for f in failed_tests(res.output)]` contains only the tests that actually ran; `BL.write_full` stores that list, and `_ci_ids` later returns it without consulting the `fail_fast` flag that `BR.candidate_ids` receives. Given `pytest --fail-fast` (or the equivalent gate knob), suppose the first failure is baseline-red `test_base` in an unchanged file, while a later test `test_item` fails only on the item. The run stops at `test_base`, the file contains `[test_base]`, `_ci_ids` returns `[test_base]`, `on_base` finds it red, the changed/imported-file check passes, and the gate auto-accepts. The new failure in `test_item` was never executed, so a fail-fast ci run is accepted as if it had measured the whole failing set.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/api/cirun.py:158 / ddflow/api/gate_baseline.py:43

chunk_findings.detail: The whole-id matcher rejects ordinary punctuation immediately around a test id, so dedup misses bugs that do name the id. For failing ids `["test_login"]`, `_names("test_login: fails on base", "test_login")` returns false because the negative lookahead disallows `:` immediately after the id; `_names("[test_login] fails", "test_login")` returns false because the negative lookbehind disallows `[` immediately before the id. In either case `_linked` does not find the open bug and `_file` files a duplicate baseline-red bug, violating the file-or-link-once behavior.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/api/gate_baseline.py:_names:99

chunk_findings.detail: `notify` persists the “told” record before sending the coordinator inbox message and then ignores the adapter result. Given `cfg.gates.baseline_red_notify_to` set and an inbox adapter that returns false (or raises), `PO.record_auto` has already written the marker into the approvals log, so `_said` will match `text in r["text"]` on the next gate run and return false without retrying `LR.notify`; if the adapter merely returns false, `notify` still returns true as though the notification succeeded. This contradicts the intended “notify the coordinator” behavior and is the previously confirmed record-before-notify/retry defect, not fixed by the current code.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/api/gate_baseline_notice.py:notify

chunk_findings.detail: `cache_store` reads the existing `ids` mapping and then builds the merged cache with a dict comprehension that evaluates `float(v[1])` for every held entry. If any held entry is from the previous cache shape (a bare boolean) or otherwise malformed, that expression raises `TypeError`/`ValueError`, the outer `except` catches it, and the function returns before calling `atomic_write`. Given a cache file at `_path(repo, sha, command)` containing `{"sha": sha, "ids": {"test_a": true}}` — the shape left by a command-keyed cache before the per-id-timestamp format — a call such as `cache_store(repo, sha, {"test_b": False}, ttl_s, command)` silently writes nothing, and `cache_load` also returns `{}` for that file. The poisoned sha/command can therefore never be migrated or updated, causing every later baseline measurement for that sha to re-run the base instead of using the cache, contrary to the stated “cached base makes measuring a comparison, not a run” intent.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/services/gates/baseline.py:cache_store

chunk_findings.detail: The new `whole` guard treats every failed run from a fail-fast command as unable to prove baseline failures, even when the chunk contains only the requested failing ids and the evidence names them. For example, with `gdef.command = "pytest -x"`, `ids = ["test_login"]`, and a base run that returns `outcome == "failed"` with `ev = {"failed_tests": ["test_login"], "failed_tests_more": False}`, `TS.fail_fast(gdef.command)` is true, so `whole` is false, `known` is never updated, and the function returns `red: False` while caching nothing. A baseline-red partial using a fail-fast gate command is therefore not auto-accepted even though the probe ran and proved the base failure, contradicting the acceptance rule that available probes may accept when all failing ids are baseline failures.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/services/gates/baseline_red.py:on_base

chunk_findings.detail: When more than one chunk is run, the returned evidence describes only the last chunk: `cmd` is the last chunk command and, when `red` is false, `outcome` is `outcomes[-1]`. Given more than `CHUNK` failing ids, if the first chunk fails on the base and the last chunk passes, the function returns `outcome: "passed"` and `command` for only the last subset, even though the baseline measurement included a failed run and possibly other chunks. This misstates the recorded baseline evidence; the outcome and command should aggregate or otherwise represent all chunks that were run.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/services/gates/baseline_red.py:on_base

chunk_findings.detail: The new tree guard is opt-out, not opt-in: the final return is `tree is None or (bool(ran) and ran == ...)`, and `tree` defaults to `None`. Given an item whose ci gate evidence is `{"baseline": {"red": True}, "tree_sha": "other-tree"}` (or lacks `tree_sha`) and a call `_ci_baseline_red(it)` / an outer call where `tree` is `None`, the function returns `True` before comparing the stored `tree_sha`. That lets `_ci_not_passed_here` be skipped and the unit_tests gate proceed on a stale baseline-red ci, contradicting the comment that “a baseline-red ci of another commit proves nothing.” The function should require a tree, a non-empty stored `tree_sha`, and equality.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/services/testscope.py:_ci_baseline_red

chunk_findings.detail: The rewritten “told once” test still does not verify the notice part after the repeated gate run. It captures `notices` before the second `_run(repo)` and never reloads them; after the second run it checks only bug identity and pending coordinator messages. If the second gate run appends another brief-line notice while inbox and bug dedup still work, the test passes, so the stated “notice and bug filed once” behavior is not actually covered for notices.
chunk_findings.title: tests/test_baseline_red_auto.py:62

chunk_findings.detail: The new fixture invokes git directly via `subprocess.run(["git", "-C", str(repo), "add", "-A"])` and `subprocess.run(["git", "-C", str(repo), "commit", ...])`, bypassing the git port required by [r-adapters]. This makes the test depend on the real git binary/ambient git configuration even when the git adapter is faked or swapped; for example, a test run that replaces the git adapter with a fake or runs where real git is unavailable/configured differently will fail in fixture setup rather than exercising the gate logic through the port. This violates the one-external-dependency-one-port rule.
chunk_findings.title: tests/test_baseline_red_auto.py:_ci_project

chunk_findings.detail: The new whole-id matcher still treats `/` as a valid trailing boundary. The negative lookahead `(?![\w\]\[:-]|\.\w)` does not exclude a following `/`, so given failing ids `["test_a"]` and an open bug summary `"test_a/helpers.py is broken"`, `re.search` matches `test_a` before the slash. `_linked` then returns that bug and `_file` is skipped, even though the bug names a path component, not the standalone test id `test_a`. This is the same substring-dedup defect as the prior `test_ab` issue, for path-separator suffixes.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/api/gate_baseline.py:_names

chunk_findings.detail: The `gate == "ci"` branch unconditionally replaces `ids` from the full failing-id file even when the current result is not `"failed"`. After a previous failed `ddflow ci run` on sha S writes the file, a later invocation of this measurement path for the same sha with `result = "passed"` and `ev["ci_scope"]["sha"] == S` still gets `ids = ["test_a", ...]` from `_ci_ids`. `if not ids: return result, why` is skipped, so the code runs `BR.on_base` and may append `new failure(s) not failing on base` to a passing result or `_file` a bug for stale failure ids. The file read should be guarded by `result == "failed"`.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/api/gate_baseline.py:gate == "ci" branch / `_ci_ids`

chunk_findings.detail: The current code still calls `PO.record_auto(...)` before attempting `LR.notify(...)`, and the updated `_said` deduplicates on the marker stored in that recorded text. Because `LR.notify`'s return value is ignored and no exception is caught, a transient coordinator inbox failure is never retried: first run records the approval, then `LR.notify` raises (or returns false); on the next run `_said(state, canon, mark)` is already true, so `notify` returns `False` before reaching `LR.notify`. Concrete input: `cfg.gates.baseline_red_notify_to` is set to `"coordinator"`, the inbox adapter is temporarily down; after it recovers, no coordinator message is ever sent. This contradicts the triage's `confirmed -- fixed: inbox sent first, approvals-log entry only after it succeeds`; this part's diff still shows the record before the notification.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/api/gate_baseline_notice.py:notify

chunk_findings.detail: `_ci_project` imports `subprocess` and runs the real Git binary directly with `subprocess.run(["git", "-C", str(repo), "add", "-A"], check=True)` and the following `git commit`. The rule says external subprocess tools/Git must go through a port in `ddflow/adapters`, and its rationale is that tests use a fake instead of a subprocess. This new fixture hits the real `git` binary directly, so a fake or adapter swap cannot intercept it, and the test becomes non-hermetic, violating [r-adapters].

chunk_findings.detail: `found["auto"] = BL.auto_decision(...)` is computed only after `_linked` / `_file`, and no branch uses it to prevent filing or linking a baseline-red bug. For example, with `[gates].baseline_red_auto = "off"` (person-only), or with it `"on"` but one failing id is in a file the item changed, `found["red"]` can still be true; `apply` still calls `_file`, creating a bug tagged `baseline-red`, then records `found["auto"]` as false. The acceptance decision must be made before any bug is filed/linked (and before returning the accepted partial reason), so a blocked acceptance can still produce an automatic baseline-red bug.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/api/gate_baseline.py:apply

chunk_findings.detail: The duplicate-suppression key is the rendered notice text, but `notice_text` truncates the failing-id list at `SHOWN = 8`. If the acceptance has more than eight ids, a change to any id beyond the first eight that leaves the total count unchanged produces exactly the same text, so `_said` treats the notice as already said and `notify` returns `False` without sending a new inbox message or recording a new log entry. For example, first acceptance has `auto.ids = ["a","b","c","d","e","f","g","h","x"]`; a later acceptance has `auto.ids = ["a","b","c","d","e","f","g","h","y"]`. Both render as `...: a, b, c, d, e, f, g, h (+1 more) fail ...`, so the second run is suppressed even though the evidence `ids` changed, contradicting the stated “told once per recorded outcome and failing ids” behavior.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/api/gate_baseline_notice.py:_said

chunk_findings.detail: The recorded reason is built as `R.render(canon, text, cfg.approvals.reason_chars) + f"\n  accepted automatically: {rule_id}"`, so the configured `reason_chars` limit is applied only to the first part of the text. The final stored reason can therefore exceed `cfg.approvals.reason_chars`, and if the approvals log re-truncates the stored reason to that limit, the appended `accepted automatically` marker (and possibly the baseline-red ids in `text`) can be cut off. For example, with `cfg.approvals.reason_chars=40` and a 45-character baseline-red reason containing test ids, the rendered part is 40 characters, the suffix makes the stored reason longer than 40, and a 40-character display truncation loses the fact that the acceptance was automatic. This violates the configured reason limit [r-everything-configurable].
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/services/approvals/policy.py:record_auto

chunk_findings.detail: The added guidance in the `ValueError` is emitted whenever `refusal(it, gate)` is empty, not only when automatic acceptance would actually happen. For example, if a gate has a measured baseline-red partial but `[gates].baseline_red_auto` is `off` (or auto-acceptance was blocked because a failing id is in a changed/imported file), `refusal` can still return empty while `auto_ids(...)` returns `[]`. An agent request that fails `CN.operator_gate` then receives “A baseline-red partial needs no request: `gate run` accepts it itself”, even though `gate run` will not accept it. That contradicts D-baseline-red-auto-accept and can cause an agent to loop instead of fixing the failure or obtaining a person approval.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/services/gate_accept.py:request_approval

chunk_findings.detail: Automatic acceptance is not tied to the current gate/item state. `accepted(state, it, gate, cfg)` returns the automatic verdict solely from stored evidence `baseline.auto.accepted` and the current config, ignoring `state` and `digest(it, gate)`, while the person path requires `AP.check(... digest(it, gate))`. If `gate run` records `baseline.auto.accepted: true` for ids `[t1]`, then the item is changed so that `t1` is now in a changed file (or a new failing test appears) and the gate evidence is not rewritten, `accepted` still returns `True`. This can let `complete` settle a stale partial, violating D-accept-baseline-red-partial’s requirement that the *current* partial be measured as baseline-red and D-baseline-red-auto-accept’s changed-file/import-graph check.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/services/gate_accept.py:auto_ids

chunk_findings.detail: `cache_store` is documented as best-effort, but its merge step trusts the existing cache file’s shape. If a local cache file contains valid JSON whose `ids` value is not a mapping (for example `{"ids": []}`) or whose entries are malformed mappings (for example `{"ids": {"a": {}}}`), the merge code raises `AttributeError` from `held.items()` or `KeyError` from `v[1]`, neither of which is caught by the outer `except (OSError, ValueError, IndexError, TypeError)`. For example, with `.ddflow/local/baseline/<sha>.<cmd>.json` containing `{"ids": []}`, calling `cache_store(repo, sha, {"tests/test_a.py::t": True}, ttl_s=60)` crashes instead of returning and forcing a rerun.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/services/gates/baseline.py:cache_store

chunk_findings.detail: The cache uses `time.time()` directly for timestamps and TTL checks, bypassing the project’s clock adapter required by [r-adapters] (“clocks” are listed as external dependencies that must go through a port). This also makes TTL enforcement depend on wall-clock time: if the system clock moves backward after a cache entry is written, `clock_now - float(v[1])` is negative and the entry is treated as fresh, so `[gates].baseline_cache_ttl_s` does not expire it. `cache_store` additionally has no injectable clock, so expiration cannot be tested deterministically.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/services/gates/baseline.py:cache_load/cache_store

chunk_findings.detail: When a chunk run returns outcome `"failed"` and no `failed_tests_more`, the code stores `False` for every id in that chunk that is not listed in `failed_tests`. That is only sound if the command executed every selected id. A gate command that stops on the first failure (`pytest -x` / `--maxfail=1`) or times out does not. With an empty baseline cache, `gdef.command = "pytest -x"`, and current failing ids `["test_a", "test_b"]` where both fail on the base, the single chunk runs `pytest -x test_a test_b`; `test_a` fails, `test_b` is not run, evidence has `failed_tests=["test_a"]` and no `failed_tests_more`. The code caches `test_b` as not failing on the base. Later, for an item failing only `test_b`, the cached branch sees `test_b` known `False` and returns `red=False`, permanently blocking a valid baseline-red acceptance. The unrun probe should be treated as unavailable/unknown, not as a passed baseline test.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/services/gates/baseline_red.py:on_base (chunk loop, `known.update` / `BL.cache_store`)

chunk_findings.detail: `_ci_baseline_red` returns true whenever the ci gate’s stored evidence has `baseline.red is True`, without checking that that evidence is for the current tree/base or that the probe actually ran for this tree. `scope` then skips `_ci_not_passed_here(cfg, it, tree)`, which is the tree-aware fallback. Concrete failure: an item previously ran ci on tree T1 and left `ci.outcome == "partial"` with `ci.evidence = {"baseline": {"red": True}}`; the item is then checked on a new tree T2 (or after the base moved) with no ci run for T2. `_ci_not_passed_here` would return a reason because the ci gate did not pass “here”, but `red` is true, so `scope` returns a selected scope for the unit_tests gate instead of the full/waiting scope. The unit_tests gate can then run only the selected scope and miss failures outside it, treating a stale/unavailable baseline probe as accepted.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/services/testscope.py:_ci_baseline_red

chunk_findings.detail: The `new` value is written as `"\"on\""`, which TOML parses to the literal string `"on"` including quote characters, not the intended knob value `on`. A consumer that uses this field as the default value or validates it against the documented `on|off` set will not match: `change["new"] == "on"` is false. The change therefore encodes a broken default for the automatic acceptance knob, so the described default-on behavior is not actually represented.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/templates/upgrade/unreleased/knob_added.gates.baseline_red_auto.toml:6

chunk_findings.detail: The `new` value is written as `"\"coordinator\""`, which TOML parses to the literal string `"coordinator"` with embedded quotes, not the recipient name `coordinator`. If the notification code or upgrade consumer compares this value to the coordinator inbox or writes it as the config value, it will not match the intended recipient. The neighboring integer `baseline_red_rate_warn` entry uses an unquoted `10`, indicating `new` is meant to be the actual value rather than a quoted TOML source fragment.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/templates/upgrade/unreleased/knob_added.gates.baseline_red_notify_to.toml:6

chunk_findings.detail: The fake baseline measurement returned by the monkeypatched `BR.on_base` is internally inconsistent with the contract exercised elsewhere in this file: it returns `{"red": False, "still_failing": ids[:-1]}`. A non-empty `still_failing` list should imply a red baseline (`test_the_base_is_run_once_per_sha_and_shared` asserts `red` is true when the baseline run has failing tests, while `test_a_run_that_could_not_run_is_not_cached_and_never_red` asserts `red` is false only for an unavailable run). If `gate_baseline.apply` honors the `red` flag, it will not treat this as a baseline-red comparison and will likely mark all current failing ids as new, so the assertion `ev["baseline"]["new_failures"] == [ids[-1]]` fails. If `apply` ignores `red` and uses `still_failing` anyway, the test passes but does not actually exercise the intended “baseline-red ci with one new failure blocks” path.
chunk_findings.title: tests/test_baseline_red_auto.py:test_ci_with_a_failure_not_on_the_base_stays_failed_and_says_so

chunk_findings.detail: The fixture invokes `subprocess.run(["git", ...])` directly to add and commit the fake project, bypassing the project’s adapter/port discipline for external dependencies and subprocess tools. This violates [r-adapters], which requires external dependencies (explicitly including git and subprocess tools) to go through `ddflow/adapters` ports and encourages tests to use fakes instead of real subprocesses.
chunk_findings.title: tests/test_baseline_red_auto.py:_ci_project

chunk_findings.detail: The new baseline write has no `full` guard. `cirun` is explicitly intended to support partial runs (`full=False`), and in a partial run `res.failures` only contains the tests that the partial scope happened to execute. The block treats that subset as a full-suite baseline by calling `BL.write_full(repo, res.sha, everyone)`. Concrete failure: a partial run on base sha `B` runs tests only for changed file `a.py`, fails `test_a`, and never runs `test_b`, which is also failing in the full suite on `B`; the cache for `B` becomes `[test_a]`. A later item based on `B` whose only failure is `test_b` is therefore blocked instead of accepted as baseline-red, violating the “one full-suite result per base sha” invariant and the promised `subset of baseline failures` acceptance.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/api/cirun.py:158-165

chunk_findings.detail: `_names` does not enforce the same boundary after the id as before it: the negative lookbehind forbids `.` and `/`, but the negative lookahead `(?![\w\]\[:-])` omits both. Concretely, `_names("test.py::test[param.with.dot]", "test.py::test[param]")` returns True because the shorter id is matched at the start and the following `.` is allowed. A pytest parameterized test can have both `test.py::test[param]` and `test.py::test[param.with.dot]` as distinct node ids; an open bug mentioning only the longer id would be treated as already naming the shorter failing id, so `_linked` reuses the wrong bug and never files the baseline-red bug for the real `test[param]` failure. The trailing boundary must forbid the same id characters as the leading boundary.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/api/gate_baseline.py:_names

chunk_findings.detail: When `notify_auto` fails to send the inbox message because `LR.notify` returns a non-empty `why` (e.g., the coordinator inbox adapter is temporarily unavailable), `notify_auto` returns `False` without recording anything, and this return value is discarded here. The gate outcome has already been recorded as accepted-baseline-red, so there is no later call to `notify_auto` unless the gate is run again. In that environment the item is accepted without the required coordinator notification, and the intended retry represented by `notify_auto`’s `False` is never acted upon.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/api/gates/_run.py:481

chunk_findings.detail: When `[gates].baseline_red_auto` is `"off"` (person-only mode) and a measured baseline-red partial is still unsettled, `refusal(it, gate)` is still falsy, so this branch appends “`gate run` accepts it itself”. But `auto_ids` only auto-accepts when the knob is `"on"`; with it off, `gate run` will not accept itself and a person must approve. This makes the error string instruct the agent to re-run a gate that will still not settle, which is wrong for that configuration.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/services/gate_accept.py:150

chunk_findings.detail: `cache_load`, `cache_store`, and `write_full` access the filesystem and system clock directly (`time.time`, `Path.read_text`, `Path.mkdir`, `atomic_write`, `fsio.ensure_ignored_dir`) instead of going through a port in `ddflow/adapters`. [r-adapters] says filesystem layout and clocks are external dependencies that must go through adapters. This implementation cannot be swapped for a fake, and the shared `.ddflow/local/baseline` read-modify-write cache has no adapter-mediated serialization, so parallel stock items can lose cache updates.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/services/gates/baseline.py:31-80

chunk_findings.detail: When the per-chunk run returns `("failed", {"failed_tests": []})` (for example a collection/infrastructure failure where no test IDs could be captured), `failing_here` is empty, and the condition `outcome in ("passed", "failed") and not ev.get("failed_tests_more")` is true, so the code stores every id in that chunk as `False` in the baseline cache. This turns an unavailable base measurement into a cached “these tests pass on the base” verdict. Later calls with those ids hit the all-cached branch and return `red=False` without re-running, blocking baseline-red auto-accept until cache TTL expiry or base movement. The code’s own comment says a run that could not run says nothing about the base; such a result must not be cached as a pass.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/services/gates/baseline_red.py:on_base

chunk_findings.detail: The new test helper invokes `subprocess.run(["git", "-C", str(repo), "add", "-A"], check=True)` and a matching `git commit` directly rather than going through the ddflow/adapters port for git/subprocess. This violates r-adapters, which requires subprocess/git access through a port and says tests should use a fake instead of a real subprocess. In an environment where the `git` CLI is absent or no user identity is configured, the commit step raises `CalledProcessError` and `_ci_project` fails, even though the code under test would otherwise behave correctly.
chunk_findings.title: tests/test_baseline_red_auto.py:_ci_project [r-adapters]

chunk_findings.detail: `_path` computes `digest(command)[:12]` on line 33, but `digest` from `ddflow.core.digest` (content_digest) expects a file path or bytes, not a string command. Passing a string like `""` or `"pytest tests/"` will raise a TypeError when it attempts to open or process the argument as bytes/Path.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/services/gates/baseline.py:33

chunk_findings.detail: The duplicate-suppression marker is computed from `content_digest(','.join(sorted(ids)))[:10]`, which is not an injective encoding of the failing-id set when an id itself contains a comma. For example, `marker("item", "ci", ["a,b", "c"])` and `marker("item", "ci", ["a", "b,c"])` both digest the string `"a,b,c"` and therefore produce the same marker. If the first acceptance is recorded, a later acceptance of the second, different failing set for the same item/gate state will have the same marker, so `_said` returns true and `notify` returns `False` without recording a new brief line or sending a new inbox message. Pytest parametrized ids can contain commas, so this is reachable; the marker should encode the list unambiguously (e.g. JSON or length-prefixed ids).
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/api/gate_baseline_notice.py:marker

chunk_findings.detail: The new `whole` guard still treats a failed base run as having executed every selected id as long as it listed *some* failure and the command is not `-x`-style fail-fast. A non-fail-fast command can still skip selected ids. For example, with a ci gate command `pytest -k "not slow"`, suppose the current item tree has `tests/test_a.py::test_a` failing and no longer marked `slow`, so it is a current failing id, and the chunk also contains `tests/test_b.py::test_b`, which fails on the base. On the base checkout `test_a` is marked `slow`, so the base run deselects `test_a`, runs `test_b`, and fails. The code sees `outcome == "failed"`, `failing_here == {"...test_b"}`, `failed_tests_more` false, and `TS.fail_fast(gdef.command)` false, so `whole` is true and it caches `test_a` as `False` (passes on the base). Later, the subset check sees `test_a` not in the baseline failing ids and refuses automatic acceptance even though `test_a` is actually baseline-red; more generally, a test that could not run on the base is recorded as having run and passed.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/services/gates/baseline_red.py:on_base

chunk_findings.detail: The new negative lookahead `(?![\w\]\[:-]|\.\w)` still permits a following `/`, so a shorter test id is treated as naming a longer pytest nodeid whose parameter contains a slash. For example, `_names("test.py::test[param/extra]", "test.py::test[param]")` returns `True` because after `test.py::test[param]` the next character is `/`, which is not blocked. Pytest allows such nodeids (`@pytest.mark.parametrize("x", ["param", "param/extra"])`), and bug dedup/linking will treat a bug naming the longer id as naming the shorter id, leading to an incorrect link or a skipped filing. The dot fix is incomplete.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/api/gate_baseline.py:100 `_names`

chunk_findings.detail: `PO.record_auto` is now called before `LR.notify`, and the return value of `LR.notify` is ignored. The durable record contains the new duplicate-suppression `marker`, so if the coordinator inbox adapter is temporarily unavailable and `LR.notify` fails (returns a non-empty `why`), the function still returns `True`; any later call sees the stored marker and is suppressed by `_said`. The item is therefore accepted without the required coordinator inbox message and no retry occurs. This is the same defect as previous finding #16: the “no record” half is fixed, but the acceptance-without-notification half still holds in this delta.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/api/gate_baseline_notice.py:notify

chunk_findings.detail: The first assertion passes `Check("command", False)` together with the failed `tests` check and then expects `BL.only_tests_failed` to be truthy. In this `Check` type, `False` means the check failed: the second assertion uses `Check("ruff check", False)` as the failed lint check that must prevent baseline-red. A failed `"command"` check is not a test failure, so `only_tests_failed` should return false for that list. As written, the test either fails against a correct predicate, or forces `only_tests_failed` to ignore failed non-test command checks and let CI with a failed command be classified baseline-red.

Given failing ids `["test_a", "test_ab"]` and an open bug summary `"test_ab fails on base"`, the condition `all(i in b.summary for i in ids)` is true because `"test_a"` is a substring of `"test_ab"`; `_linked` returns that bug and suppresses filing for `test_a`, even though the bug does not name `test_a` as a separate failing test.
